I think John Rawls provides a good liberal response to this kind of thinking. His basic idea is that a just society is the one we would all agree to live in if we had to choose from behind a "veil of ignorance." That means we don't know anything about how rich our parents are or how smart we are or whether we're born with a disability, what race, gender, religion, or sexual orientation we are, and so on. Your life situation is just a blank slate. Now what kind of society would you want to live in?

He argues we would want a robust social safety net as insurance in case life gives us a shitty hand. We would want equal rights for everyone and protections for essential civil liberties. We would still want to live in a capitalist system though a) in case we get lucky in life circumstances, and b) because a capitalist system produces more wealth overall.
